text:
Diageo Korea unveiled a limited-edition Johnnie Walker Blue Label to welcome 2027, pairing its flagship Scotch with bespoke artwork celebrating hope and new beginnings.
Released earlier this week, the special bottling is the latest chapter in Johnnie Walker’s annual zodiac collection, a series known for reimagining each year’s animal symbol through distinct artistic collaborations. The limited edition marks the Year of the Red Sheep, also referred to as the Year of the Goat.
The latest edition was created in collaboration with Jiayi Li, a Chinese artist based in Paris, whose design draws on the red sheep as a symbol of warmth, dignity and vitality.
The packaging connects the animal's gentle appearance and inner determination with Johnnie Walker's longstanding "Keep Walking" philosophy, which emphasizes perseverance and moving toward new possibilities.
The limited edition also includes a footprint kit containing an ink pad and acrylic frame, allowing parents to preserve newborns' footprints as a keepsake for babies born in 2027.
The addition is intended to make the bottle a commemorative gift for families celebrating a birth, as well as for those marking important personal milestones at the start of the new year.
Johnnie Walker Blue Label is known for its blended Scotch whisky and craftsmanship, with the zodiac collection adding distinctive packaging to the established product.
The edition is available through major retailers, convenience stores and smart-order services across Korea.
"The Johnnie Walker Blue Zodiac editions have conveyed the brand's 'Keep Walking' spirit each year by interpreting symbols of the new year through distinctive artistic designs," said Jeong Dong-hyeok, marketing executive director at Diageo Korea.
"We hope this Sheep edition, created in collaboration with artist Jiayi Li, delivers a message of hope and encouragement to those preparing for new beginnings and becomes a meaningful New Year gift through which people can share special moments with loved ones," he said.
This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times.
